parameters.label: Masa siarki wyrzuconej do atmosfery (scenariusz referencyjny modeli klimatu)
parameters.locator: artemieva2017: Abstract; rodiouchkina2025: Abstract, Table 1, Results and discussion; pierazzo1998: Abstract
parameters.notes: 325 ± 130 Gt S (3D hydrocode, ~60° obliquity, gases >25 km; used by tabor2020 and senel2023). Empirical S-isotope estimate 67 ± 39 Gt (2SD) is ~5x lower (rodiouchkina2025). Pierazzo 1998: 40-560 Gt over 10-30 km impactors; 76-127 Gt with 50 % recombination (as tabulated in rodiouchkina2025 Table 1). gulick2019 quotes '325 ± 60 Gt' - inconsistent with the primary abstract (±130). Range = 2SD low of empirical (28) to Pierazzo max (560).

parameters.label: Masa siarki — estymacja empiryczna z izotopów S w warstwie K-Pg

disagreements.topic: Mass of sulfur released by the Chicxulub impact

positions.claim: ~325 ± 130 Gt S (3D hydrocode, oblique impact; widely used in climate models).
67 ± 39 Gt S (2SD) from S concentrations and δ34S in terrestrial K-Pg layers; ~5x lower, implying a milder impact winter.
Older hydrocode estimates 40-560 Gt S; 76-127 Gt if 50 % recombination of vaporised S is assumed.
Massive S transited the stratosphere (S-MIF in ejecta) and target evaporites are nearly absent from peak-ring impactites - consistent with large degassing (no mass given).

disagreements.assessment: Unresolved. The model value depends on assumed degassing thresholds, no anhydrite EOS and no recombination (likely upper-biased); the empirical value depends on preservation of sulfate in a few terrestrial sections (possibly lower-biased). Note also a citation discrepancy: gulick2019 quotes ±60 Gt while the primary abstract gives ±130 Gt. For the simulation, run both a 325 Gt and a ~70 Gt scenario.

disagreements.topic: Sulfur speciation and residence time (rapid acid rain vs. long-lived stratospheric sulfate)

positions.claim: SO3 dominates the vapour; H2SO4 aerosol is scavenged by coarse ejecta and reaches the surface within a few days, acidifying the surface ocean.
SO2 converts to stratospheric sulfate aerosol over months, forcing ~100x Pinatubo for ≥2 yr and multi-year cooling.
S-MIF requires stratospheric photochemistry of S gases, so at least part of the S reached and resided in the stratosphere.

disagreements.assessment: Both pathways probably operated (Pope 1997 already proposed an early acid pulse plus a long-lived reservoir). The partition is not quantified; Junium 2022 provides empirical support for a stratospheric fraction.

disagreements.topic: Origin and amount of K-Pg soot

positions.claim: Global wildfires produced tens of Gt of soot coincident with the Ir layer.
A significant part of the black carbon came from target-rock hydrocarbons (0.75-2.5 Gt; or 0.5-2.6 Gt from an oil-rich target); wildfires were delayed and protracted.
No continent-wide wildfire in North America (no/below-background charcoal in six non-marine sequences).
Ignition is regional and azimuth-dependent; dry litter ignites, live fuel generally not; soot explained by syn- and post-impact fires.

disagreements.assessment: The global soot layer is well documented; its source mix is not. Robertson 2013 argues target soot is far too small to explain the inventory, Lyons 2020 that molecular signatures demand a fossil source. Treat soot mass as a scenario parameter (0.75-15+ Gt).

disagreements.topic: Intensity and duration of the re-entry thermal pulse

positions.claim: 50-150x solar for 1 to several hours; global IR pulse for several hours lethal to unsheltered animals; global fires.
Self-shielding by settling spherules limits the surface pulse to ~30 min above solar (peak 5-15 kW/m², >5 kW/m² only minutes).
Strongly asymmetric: downrange sites thousands of km away can ignite, uprange sites cannot.

disagreements.assessment: The more recent radiative-transfer models (Goldin & Melosh 2009; Morgan et al. 2013) argue against a uniform multi-hour global pulse, but Goldin & Melosh note an opaque high-altitude dust cap could override self-shielding. Simulation should treat it as spatially heterogeneous and offer both duration modes.

disagreements.topic: Dominant agent of impact-winter darkness and cooling

positions.claim: Only soot from impact-driven firestorms reduces light below the photosynthetic threshold for many months.
Fine silicate dust (0.8-8 µm) sustains darkness and photosynthetic shutdown for ~2 yr; sulfur drives the main early cooling.
Sulfate aerosols dominate long-term cooling.

disagreements.assessment: No consensus; depends on assumed emission masses (S contested, soot contested, dust mass unverified here). Within the first 24 h all three are being injected; which dominates later is beyond the simulation window.

disagreements.topic: Interpretation and data of the Tanis site

positions.claim: Event Deposit is a seismically induced seiche/surge (<1 h post-impact) with spherule fall and mass death.
Fish died during spherule fall in boreal spring (independent osteohistology + δ13C with documented data).
Spring/summer season from isotope data whose primary data and laboratory are unreported; irregularities in isotope plots.

disagreements.assessment: The seiche mechanism is plausible but not uniquely demonstrated (a tsunami would be attenuated in a WIS of unknown connectivity). Season = boreal spring is supported by During 2022; DePalma 2021 should not be used as independent evidence. Other Tanis claims circulated only in popular media are not peer-reviewed and are excluded.

disagreements.topic: Gulf of Mexico K-Pg event deposits (El Mimbral, Brazos, Beloc) and timing of the impact

positions.claim: Single Chicxulub impact at the K-Pg boundary; clastic units are impact ejecta reworked by tsunami/seiche/backwash within hours-days.
Units are turbidites/lowstand deposits and Chicxulub predates the K-T boundary by ~300 kyr.

disagreements.assessment: The single-impact, boundary-coincident interpretation is the broad consensus (Schulte et al. 2010; impact within 33 kyr of the extinction per Renne et al. 2013). Details (one vs several waves; tsunami vs gravity flows) remain debated site by site.

disagreements.topic: Western Interior Seaway at the K-Pg boundary

positions.claim: PaleoDEM Map16 shows no continuous seaway; the North American interior is lowland (0-200 m).

A restricted seaway persisted through the latest Cretaceous in the western Great Plains/Dakotas (marine tongues in the Hell Creek Fm), expanding as the Paleocene Cannonball Sea; southern connections unknown.

disagreements.assessment: A residual northern seaway is supported by marine fossils, but a continuous Gulf-to-Arctic corridor at 66 Ma is not demonstrated. At 1° the DEM cannot resolve narrow marine tongues; mark as uncertain on the map.

disagreements.topic: Global sea level at the K-Pg boundary

positions.claim: ~60-70 m above present for 58-66 Ma (δ18O-Mg/Ca; flagged as suspect before 48 Ma); long-term Cretaceous peak 100 ± 50 m.
Haq-type eustatic curves are higher; PaleoDEM authors find Haq too high and Miller 2005 too low, best fit with Haq reduced by 30-40 %.

disagreements.assessment: Use ~+60-70 m as a working value with wide uncertainty; the PaleoDEM already embeds its own shoreline choices, so do not add a separate sea-level offset to the DEM.

openQuestions: Total fine-dust mass injected (Senel et al. 2023 main text inaccessible; figures circulating in press coverage were NOT used) - needs verification from the paper.

No published explicit 'darkness onset' time: models assume soot injection 12-36 h (Bardeen 2017), re-entry 25/55/85 % at 2/8/72 h (Kring & Durda 2002). Hourly surface-PAR output for the first 72 h would be needed (Bardeen 2017 SI has 1-week hourly runs - check Fig. S1/S8 data on request).
